{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"Three knocks came from the other side, slow and deliberate.

Tomas lowered his hand. “Someone’s trapped in there.”

“Or waiting,” said the child.

The paper boat drifted back toward them, though the passage sloped away. A dark drop of water trembled on its folded prow. When it touched the floor, every scratched name on the tiles flashed blue.

Mara’s name burned brightest.

The watch pulled against her palm, its chain stretching toward the keyhole. She felt the same tug in her ribs, as if the bell’s last note had become a hook.

“Don’t open it,” Tomas said. His voice sounded smaller than before. “What if it’s the thing that wrote our names?”

Another knock. Then a whisper slipped through the iron: “Mara.”

The child’s face went pale. “It knows which side you’re on.”

Mara leaned close to the door. “Who are you?”

For a moment, only the water answered, pattering in the dark. Then came a voice she knew—not from memory, but from the watch’s silver face, where it had sometimes murmured in dreams.

“I’m the part you left behind.”

Tomas seized her shoulder. “You don’t have to listen.”

But the iron door had begun to warm beneath her fingers. The keyhole widened, stretching into a narrow, bright eye.

Mara saw a room beyond it: a flooded tower chamber, a cracked window, and a little girl standing ankle-deep in black water. The girl wore Mara’s red scarf.

The child lifted the paper boat. “If you open it, the river will remember its way.”

“Remember where?” Tomas asked.

The girl beyond the door pressed her palm to the other side.

Home, Mara thought—and turned the watch’s tiny key."}
